​Dogathon — AI Valley × PetZen 🐶

​A hackathon where every project has a real dog on the other end of it.

​200 developers, designers, AI builders, vet techs, and shelter volunteers are coming together to build tools that directly support rescue operations and dog adoption.

​The day begins with rescue dogs meeting participants on-site. Teams will then spend the rest of the hackathon building products that help shelters, rescues, fosters, adopters, and dogs themselves — from adoption matching tools and volunteer coordination systems to AI copilots for rescue operations.

About Event

​Get warmed up for Actuate the best way possible—by building!

​Join Nebius, NVIDIA, Antioch, and Toloka for a day of workshops, rapid experimentation, and building at the intersection of AI and the physical world.

​We’ll begin with technical workshops designed to help you get familiar with the tools, infrastructure, and challenge space. Then, you’ll form a team—or work independently—and spend the rest of the day building a working prototype.

​What to expect

​Robotics workshops

​A focused physical AI challenge

​Access to tools, infrastructure, and technical support

​Project demos and judging

​Prizes for the strongest submissions

​Schedule (*subject to change)

​8:00am: Doors open and check-in, grab breakfast

​9:00am:  Welcome and challenge briefing

​9:15am: Technical workshops by Hosts

​10:30: Hacking begins

​12:00pm: Lunch

​1:00pm: Hacking continues

​3:30pm: Submission deadline

​4:30pm Demos and judging (top 6 live demos)

​5:30pm: Winner announcement

​6pm-9pm: happy hour (more details to come!)

​The challenge

​The Perception-Reasoning-Action Loop

​Modern AI excels at generating text and pixels, but Physical AI requires closing the loop between the digital mind and the physical embodiment. Participants will build solutions that seamlessly integrate three core pillars:

​Perception (Sense): Ingesting and interpreting multi-modal sensor data such as RGB-D video, LiDAR, IMU readings, tactile feedback, or spatial audio to build a real-time, dynamic understanding of the physical surroundings.

​Reasoning (Think): Leveraging advanced foundation models, spatial computing, and decision-making frameworks to analyze constraints, anticipate outcomes, plan multi-step tasks, and adapt to unexpected real-world changes.

​Action (Act): Translating high-level cognitive plans into precise physical outputs, including robotic manipulation, autonomous navigation, drone flight dynamics, or interactive IoT actuator responses.

​Prizes

​Prizes will include compute credits and other resources from our event partners, including $500 in Toloka platform credits, $500 in Nebius AI Cloud credits, $5k in Antioch cloud credits, and more to come!

​The full prize package will be announced soon!

​What to bring

​Bring your laptop, charger, and anything else you rely on for a full day of building. We’ll share any required setup instructions and recommended tools with registered participants before the event.

​Who should attend

​This event is designed for:

​Robotics engineers

​Machine learning engineers

​Computer vision engineers

​Research engineers and applied scientists

​Data and infrastructure engineers working with robotics or physical AI

​Technical founders and builders exploring embodied intelligence

​You don’t need to arrive with a team. We’ll help participants connect and form teams before and at the event.

​Hosted by

​Nebius · NVIDIA · Antioch · Toloka

​Important notes

​Space is limited, and all attendees must apply and be approved to attend.

​This is a hands-on technical event. Participants should be comfortable writing code and building independently or as part of a small team.

​Please register individually, even if you plan to attend with a team.

About Event

​Build in Less than a Day. Showcase on a Global Stage.

​The next generation of AI apps are built on systems that can remember, retrieve context, and take action over real application data. In this mini-hackathon, build AI applications powered by agent memory, where models work with databases, APIs, documents, code, and business systems to maintain and improve state and context over time. Agents need memory, state, context, and retrieval, and MongoDB gives you all of it on a single platform, so there’s no need for a third-party vector store, cache, or connector to bolt on. Whether you are creating autonomous developer tools, adaptive copilots, operational dashboards, or entirely new AI experiences, explore what becomes possible when intelligence is grounded in persistent memory and the right data at the right time, all in one place.

​Participants will join us on-site at Build Fest for a dedicated ~4-hour hacking block.

​Those finalists demo on-stage for attendees of Build Fest, and the audience will cast their votes in real-time.

​A winner will be crowned on the spot, right before Loud Luxury takes the stage.

​$15,000 in total prize money

​VENUE IS 18+

Want to be a judge? Apply here, open till August 18th: https://forms.gle/mMP7PxkFbpQ6dZby8

We're heading to Japantown for a full day of building, brought to you by ClickHouse! :)

One day. Real problems. Real prizes. Pick a track, form a team of up to 5 (or go solo), and build something using ClickHouse + Postgres — OLAP and OLTP, like PB&J. This is an AI hackathon grounded in problems that affect everyday people: kids who can't read, adults who are lonely, a planet people want to help but don't know how. Build something someone would actually open on a hard day.

Partner engineers will be at the expert bar all day to help you move fast. Breakfast, lunch, and drinks are on us. We close the night with demos, judging, and dinner together.

Four tracks to build in

​The reading crisis
Two-thirds of 4th graders read below grade level, and the kids furthest behind are falling fastest. Build the tool that helps a teacher spot who's quietly struggling, helps a student find the book they'll actually finish, or helps a library know what's working.

​The loneliness epidemic

​Your projects will be judged by engineers from Anthropic!

​1. Plan and Track in Port

​3. Monitor and Observe with SigNoz

​Add observability to your application or pipeline using SigNoz:

​Track traces, metrics, and logs for your data pipeline and API endpoints.

​Monitor performance latency, data execution rates, and failure events when scrapers break or auto-repair.

​Capture execution events so you always know how your system performs under the hood.

​Port.io (Project Organization)

​Port acts as your central project dashboard. It helps you organize what you are building, record technical decisions, track project risks, and list all your finished components in one place.

​Bright Data Scraper Studio is an AI-powered data extraction platform designed to turn any website into structured, machine-readable JSON feeds. Traditional web scraping often requires developers to manually maintain selector logic, handle headless browser instances, configure proxy rotation networks, and continuously update code when site DOM structures change. Scraper Studio streamlines this workflow by combining automated code generation, proxy infrastructure, and self-healing mechanisms into a unified runtime manageable directly from terminal coding agents like Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex.

​SigNoz (Full-Stack Observability)

​SigNoz is an open-source observability platform. It gives you deep visibility into your application by tracking metrics, traces, and logs so you can monitor pipeline performance and debug errors instantly.

​The Challenge

​What was the hardest part about coming home as a veteran?

​For many veterans, the challenge does not end when they leave the service. It begins when they try to navigate the systems designed to support them.

​Too often, veterans face:

​Confusing websites and complicated processes

​Long application forms

​Unclear pathways to finding the right resources

​Waiting weeks or months for support when they need it most

​When a veteran needs help, accessing support should not feel like another battle.

​Listen first, then build.

​Build AI Agents That Remember

​Join Mastra and Elastic for a hands-on hack night exploring agent memory.

​Most AI agents start every conversation from scratch. They forget what a user told them, repeat suggestions that already failed, lose track of progress, and sometimes rely on outdated information instead of what happened most recently.

​At this hack night, you’ll build an agent that can use information from the past to make better decisions in the present.

​Your agent might remember:

​A user’s preferences

​What has already been tried

​Progress toward a goal

​Previous decisions and their rationale

​Important events or changes

​What should happen next

​You’ll also explore an important memory challenge: not everything from the past should be treated equally. Recent information may be more relevant than older information, and a new decision may need to replace or outweigh an outdated one.

​After a short introduction and demo, we’ll spend the rest of the evening building.

​The stack

​Mastra

​Mastra is an open-source TypeScript framework for building AI agents. It handles the agent loop, tools, memory, and workflows, so you can focus on what your agent should do instead of wiring up LLM calls by hand.

​Elasticsearch

​Elasticsearch provides the retrieval and memory layer. You can use it as Mastra’s native vector store or explore hybrid search, which combines keyword and semantic matching to help your agent find the right context.

​What can you build?

​Build anything that becomes more useful when it can access relevant information or remember what happened before.

​A few ideas:

​A learning coach that remembers a student’s progress

​A customer-support assistant that knows what has already been tried

​A research agent that tracks sources, findings, and open questions

​A travel planner that remembers preferences and past feedback

​A project assistant that recalls decisions and next steps

​A creative collaborator that maintains continuity across sessions

​Bring your own data, use one of our starter datasets, or begin with one of the examples provided.

​AI agents are easy to prototype and much harder to run in production. Once an agent touches real users, tools, data, budgets, and internal systems, the work becomes less about a clever prompt and more about routing, permissions, tracing, retries, evals, guardrails, cost controls, and deployment.

​Join TrueFoundry and HackerSquad for a full-day Agent Harness hackathon focused on building production-minded agentic applications. The goal is simple: take an agent use case from idea or prototype toward something that can be observed, governed, evaluated, and operated.

​TrueFoundry's AI Gateway, Agent Gateway, and MCP Gateway will frame the day. Builders will work on practical agent harness patterns such as model routing, controlled tool access, MCP workflows, observability, eval loops, fallback behavior, budget controls, governance, and deployment paths.

​Agent systems need to coordinate models, tools, permissions, memory, context, retries, and fallbacks without becoming brittle one-off glue code.

​Guardrails need to become runtime controls: clear rules for what data an agent can see, which tools it can call, which actions require human approval, and how unsafe requests or outputs get blocked, logged, or escalated.

​Deployment gets harder when agents need to connect to internal systems, respect governance rules, and stay reliable as usage grows.

Media is becoming iterative.
For a century, a film was a finished thing. Made once, shipped once, watched. That is ending. The new model is media that gets made, remixed, and reshaped continuously, by small teams using tools that turn an idea into a finished frame in an afternoon.
Film is one of the biggest mediums this reshapes, and we want to bring the people rebuilding it in one room.
This September we're hosting a generative AI short film hackathon in San Francisco, with Machine Cinema, the most active community of AI filmmakers working today.
The format is simple. About 20 teams of three or four. A few hours to make and premiere a one to three minute animated short, using the latest tooling across video, image, audio, and world models.
A medium doesn't move forward in essays about it. It moves forward when the people defining it are in the same room, making things.
Come build with us!

candidates.title: The Next Interface Hackathon: Rethink how we talk to AI
candidates.evidence:
The Next Interface Hackathon: Rethink how we talk to AI
For three years, using AI meant typing into a box and waiting for text to come back.
That era is ending. 

The next interface isn't a chat window. It's worn, spoken, and always on.
Glasses that listen.
A pendant that remembers. 
A tracker you never charge. 
A second self that watches your screen and acts before you ask.
We're putting the founders building that future in one room with the people who want to build on it.

Half a day in San Francisco. 

Real hardware on the table. Working demos, not slideware.
The lineup is a short list of founders shipping the wearables that are pulling AI off the screen. 

The founders in the room:
Adam Cohen Hillel, Secondly - a personal AI "second self" that sees your screen and acts across every app you use. The chat box becomes a presence.
Nik Shevchenko, Omi - the open-source AI wearable necklace, with 250+ developer apps already built on it. Always listening, always yours.
AnhPhu Nguyen, Mira - AI smart glasses with no camera. They hear what you hear, recall every name, and translate 60+ languages in under a second. AnhPhu is the Harvard builder behind last year's viral I-XRAY demo.
Andy Kong, Chargerless - a 7-gram health tracker powered by daylight. One minute of sun a day and it never needs a charger.
What you'll build: pick a device, an API, or a live sensor stream. 

Ship something a person could actually wear or talk to by the time we demo.

 The strongest builds demo to the founders in the room.
This is for builders, hardware hackers, AI engineers, and designers who think the keyboard is a temporary technology.
